Summer classes move quick, so you can’t wait until test week to find out what you remember. Stop relying on passive review and start using active recall. Pull the information from memory without your notes. Don’t just look over the material. Practice explaining it. And one of the easiest ways to do this is flashcards. But don’t just flip and recognize answers. Use them like cue cards. Ask why, what, and how. Make yourself answer before flipping, even if you’re struggling. Separate what you get right and wrong, and keep repeating the ones you miss. Then space it out: review one day later, then three days, then seven. In a summer class, consistency matters even more.
